quotes.text: A role applies to the whole workspace, not to a single report. There's no switch that lets someone edit this dashboard while only reading that one, because the seat covers everything inside the room.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains clearly that workspace roles are scoped to the whole workspace, not to items.

quotes.text: An app is a delivery layer, not a data lock. It decides what a person can open, not which rows of data they see.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A crisp distinction between content distribution and data security.

quotes.text: Get the role wrong and the wrong person walks into the room. Get the row rules wrong and the right person sees the wrong numbers.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorably contrasts the two failure modes of roles and row-level security.

quotes.text: The biggest one is handing out admin because deciding feels slow. It's the easiest role to give and the hardest one to take back, since only an admin can change another person's role.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the most common beginner mistake with a concrete reason to avoid it.

chapters.title: The four seats: viewer to admin
The viewer sees more than you think

takeaways: Power BI workspaces have four stacked roles (viewer, contributor, member, admin), and each role applies to the entire workspace rather than to single reports.
A viewer can open everything in a workspace, so keep drafts out of viewer-facing workspaces and use links or apps for narrower sharing.
Workspace roles control who gets in, while row-level security in the semantic model controls which rows each person sees, and in shared capacity every user needs a paid license.
hook: Most teams hand out Power BI workspace roles in one click and only later discover who can see, edit or delete what. This episode explains the four roles, the licensing catch and the difference between roles and row-level security for anyone setting up Power BI for a team. You will know which seat fits each teammate and where a role stops protecting your data.
